Four moves from phone to link.

Tap any step below to jump the live diagram.

  1. Hold your iPhone upright and turn slowly until the ring closes at each spot.

  2. Tap Finish & save, check the route checks, then tap Send to Veylet. Send from the app: it uploads in the background. Check your account for rendering status.

  3. An automatic quality check assesses capture quality, then we’ll email you when it’s ready to preview on your phone.

  4. Tap Approve and share for a browser link, open-home QR code, website embed, and listing videos.

Quick reference & FAQs.

First-session checklist & room counting details
  1. Install and sign in. Use Apple or the email you joined with. Install the app and sign in.
  2. Practise or start straight away. When your account is admitted, you can try an optional practice room first or go straight to capturing a space room by room. The practice room.
  3. Check rooms & privacy before leaving. Clear private documents, read the route checks, and tap Send to Veylet. What each status means.
  4. Review before sharing. A tour uses the rooms counted in it (how rooms are counted) only after it passes the automatic quality check and you tap Approve and share. Turn sharing off anytime in your account, or ask Veylet support.
What if the first result is not usable?

An automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work; other findings are flagged for you to check before approval. If your first walkthrough isn’t listing-ready, we redo it free: the redo corrects it on the same link and uses no rooms, though a new capture visit is not included. Keep the originals and report the affected area. After that, we agree a correction, a permitted whole recapture including every original room or the remedy in your scope. A correction or permitted whole recapture replaces the walkthrough on the same link and uses no rooms; any other new accepted capture is its own walkthrough and link, and uses its own rooms. Sharing waits for review and approval.

Can every visitor open a tour?

Visitors use a current browser with graphics support on a phone, tablet or computer. Performance depends on the tour, device and connection. Share a direct link as a fallback for website builders that block embedded content. Portal compatibility must be checked with that portal.

Can an agency use it free?

Eligible App Store subscribers receive 1 free month with 30 rooms in total. It begins when the plan is activated with a payment method on file, and there is one trial per agency (ABN) and workspace. The first charge is on the day it ends; cancel before then and nothing is charged. App Store subscriptions renew at the price of the plan you chose, monthly or yearly, unless cancelled through Apple. Invoiced service continues only under explicitly agreed and settled terms; it does not auto-renew. On the monthly Veylet plan each paid month includes 30 rooms, the same as the free month, and unused ones carry over, up to 40 banked; the yearly plan has 360 rooms to use any time in the plan year. Top-up packs for busier months aren’t on sale yet. Check the renewal date on your account; you can cancel any time. Every walkthrough you released stays live while your plan runs; when it ends, its links keep working for 14 days, then go offline until you restart it. While capture quality is still being proven we onboard accounts in cohorts, so ask about availability before promising a client a date.

Is a walkthrough a measured survey?

No. It provides visual context for a space. It is not a measured floor plan, building survey or guarantee of condition. Keep listing photography and required property information available alongside it.
